# LB1 / 1st Place — Gap analysis (us vs the 1st-place writeup)

> "our approach" cites `competitions/nvidia-nemotron/{notes,submissions,tracking,insights,equation-frontier,bugs}.md`.
> "writeup" cites `../writeup/lb1-writeup.md` (= `temp/LB1.pdf`). Where the repo records nothing, says `unknown`.
> Our best: **soup (v14+c1+b1) Public 0.86 / Private 0.85**; post-deadline **eq-aug 0.86/0.86**. LB1: **Public 0.91 / Private 0.920**. The gap is ~+0.07 private, concentrated in cryptarithm + bit.

## Why our EQ1..EQ4 / T12 / replay / synthetic / merge attempts did not close the gap

- **EQ1..EQ4 (equation):** We framed equation-numeric as a **global deterministic cipher / PRF** unrecoverable from samples (EQ-0/EQ-2′), so we pursued **coverage-memorization** of seen inputs (eq-aug 0.86/0.86) rather than per-prompt operator inference. LB1's coverage table shows **equation-numeric *deduce* is ~95% solvable** via the 24-rule inventory + Obs.1/Obs.2 *per prompt*. The likely error: equation-numeric is **per-prompt operator rules**, the same structure as cryptarithm-without-symbol-hiding — not one global function. Our "guess" pessimism may have been correct only for the **unseen-operator** subset (their guess = 52%). **Action: re-run an EQ probe assuming per-prompt 24-rule operators.** (equation-frontier.md:135-228)
- **T12 hard-val:** Built too late and mispredicts atypical adapters, so it couldn't steer the campaign; it confirmed soup/v14 but didn't surface the cryptarithm/bit method gap. (submissions.md:76-78)
- **replay (v14, +0.18):** The single biggest *generic* lever (clean recipe), but it plateaus at the SFT ceiling (~0.86) — it does not solve cryptarithm/bit. (tracking.md:41)
- **synthetic (b1/b2/v15/c1/c2):** Too small and **diluting** — regressed the hardest cipher/bit slice to ≤ base, because we lacked HEX (token blowup) and a memorizable catalog (no structural gain). (submissions.md:31)
- **merge / soup (0.86):** A ceiling-pusher that averages adapters; useful at 0.86 but cannot manufacture cryptarithm/bit capability that no parent has. soup_v2 even fell below parents. (submissions.md:79-82)

## High-value vs not-worth-it (for future competitions)

**High value (do):** HEX trace compression (cheap, generic for bit/long-string tasks); memorizable per-signature catalogs for symbolic-arithmetic tasks; rule-sequence catalogs + nearest-neighbor repair for bounded-combinatorial tasks; treating the **token budget as the primary design constraint** and measuring "correct within budget"; large-scale rule-enforced programmatic synth as the backbone (not bolt-on).

**Too expensive / not worth (skip or defer):** 119h main + 51h extra single-GPU SFT during a live competition (infra-bound; infeasible on ≤8h Kaggle kernels — only partially reproducible post-comp on RTX Pro 6000); RL (LB1 won without it); `lm_head` in LoRA targets (vLLM ignores it); model souping as a primary strategy (ceiling-pusher only).
